name: Sheet-Pan Lemon Chicken & Veggies
description: One pan, five boxed lunches. Juicy thighs roasted with broccoli and peppers.
steps: Heat oven to 220°C / 425°F and line a large sheet pan with parchment.
Cut chicken thighs into large bite-sized pieces so they cook at the same rate as the vegetables.
In a large bowl, whisk oil, lemon juice and zest, garlic, oregano, 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper.
Toss chicken, broccoli, peppers and onion in the marinade until everything is coated.
Spread in a single layer (use two pans if crowded) and roast 25–30 minutes, flipping once, until chicken reaches 74°C / 165°F and the edges char.
Cool 10 minutes, then divide into containers.
storage: Airtight containers in the fridge for up to 4 days.
reheat: Microwave 2 minutes, or 10 minutes in a 180°C / 350°F oven to keep the broccoli crisp.
tips: Thighs stay juicier than breasts after reheating.
Serve over rice, quinoa or in a wrap to change it up through the week.

name: Teriyaki Chicken Rice Bowls
description: Sticky homemade teriyaki over brown rice with steamed broccoli.
steps: Cook rice according to package directions (about 25 minutes for brown rice).
Whisk soy sauce, honey, vinegar, garlic, ginger, cornstarch and ¼ cup water in a small bowl.
Brown chicken in a hot oiled skillet for 5–6 minutes until cooked through.
Pour in the sauce and simmer 2–3 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Steam broccoli for 4 minutes so it stays bright green.
Assemble bowls with rice, chicken and broccoli; top with carrots, scallions and sesame seeds.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Keep extra sauce in a small separate container.
reheat: Sprinkle a teaspoon of water over the rice and microwave 2–2½ minutes.
tips: Undercook the broccoli slightly; it finishes softening when reheated.
Swap the honey for maple syrup if you prefer.

name: Turkey Taco Bowls
description: Cilantro-lime rice, spiced turkey, beans and corn.
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can black beans, rinsed and drained
steps: Cook rice; when done, fluff and stir in lime juice and cilantro.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown turkey, breaking it up, about 7 minutes.
Add chili powder, cumin, ½ tsp salt and a splash of water; simmer 2 minutes.
Warm beans and corn together in the same pan or the microwave.
Divide rice, turkey, beans, corn and tomatoes into containers.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Pack tomatoes in a corner so they don't make the rice soggy.
reheat: Microwave 2 minutes, then add tomatoes, salsa or avocado after heating.
tips: Add a spoon of salsa or Greek yogurt on the day you eat it.
Ground chicken or lean beef work just as well.

name: Beef & Broccoli
description: Takeout-style beef and broccoli that reheats beautifully.
steps: Cook jasmine rice.
Slice beef thinly against the grain (15 minutes in the freezer makes this easier) and toss with cornstarch.
Mix soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, ginger and ⅓ cup water.
Sear beef in batches over high heat, 1–2 minutes per side; set aside.
Stir-fry broccoli 3 minutes, add the sauce and beef, and simmer 2 minutes until glossy.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve over rice.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days.
reheat: Microwave 2 minutes, stirring halfway.
tips: Flank steak is a cheaper alternative to sirloin.

name: Garlic-Dill Salmon with Sweet Potato & Asparagus
description: Omega-3 rich sheet-pan dinner.
steps: Heat oven to 200°C / 400°F.
Toss sweet potatoes with half the oil and a pinch of salt; roast 10 minutes.
Push potatoes to the edges, add salmon and asparagus to the pan and drizzle with the remaining oil.
Top salmon with garlic, dill, lemon slices, salt and pepper.
Roast 12–15 minutes more until salmon flakes easily (52–60°C / 125–140°F).
storage: Fridge up to 3 days — fish is best eaten early in the week.
reheat: Microwave at 50% power for 2 minutes, or eat the salmon cold over greens.
tips: Slightly undercook the salmon so it doesn't dry out when reheated.

name: Chickpea Coconut Curry
description: Creamy vegan curry with spinach over basmati rice.
steps: Start the rice.
Sauté onion in a little oil for 5 minutes until soft; add garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in curry powder and toast 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chickpeas, tomatoes and coconut milk; simmer 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in spinach until wilted and season with salt.
Serve with basmati rice.
storage: Fridge up to 5 days. Freeze the curry (without rice) for up to 3 months.
reheat: Microwave 2–3 minutes, or thaw overnight and warm on the stove with a splash of water.
tips: A squeeze of lime right before eating brightens the leftovers.

name: Lemony Red Lentil Soup
description: Hearty, cheap and freezes well.
steps: Sauté onion, carrot and celery in a little oil for 6–8 minutes until soft.
Add garlic and cumin and cook 1 minute.
Add lentils, broth and tomatoes; bring to a boil, then simmer 20 minutes until the lentils collapse.
Blend partly with an immersion blender for a creamier texture (optional).
Stir in spinach and lemon juice; season to taste.
storage: Fridge up to 5 days, or freeze in portions for up to 3 months.
reheat: Microwave 3 minutes, adding water if it has thickened.
tips: Use vegetable broth to make it vegan.

name: Peanut Butter Banana Overnight Oats
description: No-cook breakfast jars for the whole week.
steps: Mash bananas in a large bowl.
Whisk in almond milk, peanut butter and honey until smooth.
Stir in oats and chia seeds.
Divide into 4 jars and refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight.
storage: Fridge up to 5 days.
reheat: Eat cold, or microwave 1 minute if you prefer it warm.
tips: Add a splash of milk in the morning if it's too thick.

name: Spinach & Feta Egg Muffins
description: Grab-and-go breakfast bites.
steps: Heat oven to 180°C / 350°F and grease a 12-cup muffin tin well.
Whisk eggs, milk, ½ tsp salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Divide spinach, pepper, green onions and feta between the cups.
Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables, filling each cup about ¾ full.
Bake 20–22 minutes until set in the center; cool 5 minutes before removing.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days, or freeze individually wrapped for up to 2 months.
reheat: Microwave 30–45 seconds (60–90 seconds from frozen).
tips: Silicone muffin cups make removal much easier.

name: Greek Chicken Quinoa Bowls
description: Bright, crunchy bowls with tzatziki-style yogurt sauce.
steps: Simmer quinoa in 2 cups water for 15 minutes; rest 5 minutes covered and fluff.
Toss chicken with oil, oregano, half the garlic, half the lemon juice and salt.
Grill or pan-sear 6–7 minutes per side until 74°C / 165°F; rest 5 minutes and slice.
Stir yogurt with the remaining garlic and lemon juice for the sauce.
Assemble bowls with quinoa, chicken, cucumber, tomatoes, olives, onion and feta.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Keep the yogurt sauce in a separate small container.
reheat: Warm just the chicken and quinoa for 1 minute, then add the cold toppings and sauce.
tips: Pound the chicken to an even thickness so it cooks evenly.

name: Shrimp Fried Rice
description: Better than takeout and ready in 20 minutes.
ingredients: 1 lb raw prawns, peeled and deveined
steps: Scramble eggs in a hot oiled wok until just set; set aside.
Cook shrimp 1–2 minutes per side until pink; set aside.
Stir-fry carrots, peas and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add cold rice, pressing it against the pan, and fry 3–4 minutes until hot and slightly crisp.
Stir in soy sauce and sesame oil, then fold in eggs, shrimp and scallions.
storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate within an hour; keeps 3 days.
reheat: Microwave 2 minutes until steaming hot all the way through.
tips: Day-old rice is essential: fresh rice turns mushy.

name: Turkey Meatballs with Zucchini Noodles
description: Lighter spaghetti night with half zoodles, half pasta.
steps: Heat oven to 200°C / 400°F and line a sheet pan.
Mix turkey, breadcrumbs, egg, parmesan, garlic and seasoning with your hands; don't overwork it.
Roll into 16 meatballs and bake 18 minutes.
Meanwhile cook spaghetti until al dente and drain.
Simmer meatballs in marinara for 5 minutes.
Toss the raw zucchini noodles with the hot pasta and divide into containers with meatballs and sauce.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freeze meatballs in sauce (without noodles) for up to 3 months.
reheat: Microwave 2½ minutes; the zucchini noodles soften as they heat.
tips: Pat the zucchini noodles dry so they don't water down the sauce.

name: Sweet Potato Black Bean Chili
description: Smoky vegan chili that gets better by day three.
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can black beans, rinsed and drained
1 (15 oz) can kidney beans, rinsed and drained
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté onion and pepper for 5 minutes.
Add chili powder and cumin and cook 1 minute.
Add sweet potatoes, beans, tomatoes and broth; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer 30 minutes until the sweet potatoes are tender.
Mash a few sweet potato cubes against the side of the pot to thicken.
storage: Fridge up to 5 days, or freeze in portions for up to 3 months.
reheat: Microwave 3 minutes, stirring halfway.
tips: Top with avocado, lime and cilantro when serving.

name: Peanut Tofu Noodle Bowls
description: Crispy tofu, crunchy veg and a punchy peanut-lime sauce.
ingredients: 14 oz extra-firm tofu, pressed and cubed
steps: Press tofu for 15 minutes, then cube it.
Bake at 220°C / 425°F for 25 minutes, or pan-fry until crisp on all sides.
Cook noodles per package directions; rinse under cold water so they don't stick.
Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, lime and sriracha with 3–4 tbsp warm water until pourable.
Toss noodles with sauce, cabbage, carrots and edamame; top with tofu and cilantro.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Store extra sauce separately to loosen the noodles later.
reheat: Best cold or at room temperature, like a noodle salad.
tips: Toss the noodles with a teaspoon of oil before storing so they don't clump.

name: Roasted Eggplant & Farro Salad
description: Nutty grain salad with tahini-lemon dressing.
steps: Heat oven to 220°C / 425°F.
Toss eggplant with oil and salt and roast 25 minutes, stirring halfway, until golden.
Simmer farro in salted water for 25–30 minutes until chewy-tender; drain.
Whisk tahini, lemon juice, a pinch of salt and 3 tbsp water until smooth.
Toss farro, eggplant, tomatoes, onion and parsley with the dressing.
storage: Fridge up to 5 days. It tastes better on day two.
reheat: Serve cold or at room temperature.
tips: Soak the sliced onion in cold water for 10 minutes to mellow it.

name: Maple-Dijon Pork with Brussels Sprouts & Apples
description: Autumn sheet-pan with sweet-savory glaze.
steps: Heat oven to 220°C / 425°F.
Whisk mustard, maple syrup, oil, salt and pepper.
Brush half the glaze over the pork; toss sprouts and apples with the rest and the thyme.
Arrange everything on a sheet pan, sprouts cut side down.
Roast 22–25 minutes until the pork reaches 63°C / 145°F.
Rest pork 5 minutes before slicing.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days.
reheat: Microwave 1½–2 minutes at 70% power so the pork stays tender.
tips: Firm apples like Honeycrisp or Granny Smith hold their shape.

name: Lemon Butter Cod with Potatoes & Green Beans
description: Light, flaky fish with buttery potatoes.
steps: Heat oven to 200°C / 400°F.
Toss potatoes with a tablespoon of the butter and salt; roast 15 minutes.
Mix the remaining butter with garlic and lemon juice.
Add cod and green beans to the pan and spoon the lemon butter over everything.
Roast 10–12 minutes until the cod flakes; finish with parsley.
storage: Fridge up to 3 days.
reheat: Microwave at 50% power for 2 minutes so the fish doesn't turn rubbery.
tips: Any firm white fish works: haddock, halibut or pollock.

name: Berry Yogurt Parfait Jars
description: Layered breakfast jars; keep granola separate to stay crunchy.
steps: Stir honey into the yogurt.
Layer yogurt and berries in 4 jars.
Pack granola and walnuts together in small separate containers.
Add the topping right before eating.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days.
reheat: No reheating — eat cold.
tips: Frozen berries work too; they thaw into a jammy layer overnight.

name: Slow Cooker Beef & Barley Stew
description: Set it in the morning, portion it at night.
steps: Season beef with salt and pepper and brown in batches in a hot skillet (optional but worth it).
Add beef, vegetables, barley, tomato paste and thyme to the slow cooker.
Pour in the broth and stir.
Cook on low 8 hours or high 4–5 hours until the beef is fork-tender.
Remove thyme stems and adjust seasoning.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days, or freeze in portions for up to 3 months.
reheat: Microwave 3 minutes, adding broth or water — the barley keeps absorbing liquid.
tips: No slow cooker? Simmer covered on the stove for 2 hours.

name: Spicy Tuna Rice Bowls
description: Pantry-friendly sushi-bowl vibes.
steps: Rinse sushi rice until the water runs clear, then cook it.
Mix tuna with mayonnaise, sriracha and a teaspoon of soy sauce.
Divide rice, spicy tuna, cucumber and edamame into containers.
Add avocado and nori strips just before eating so they stay fresh.
storage: Fridge up to 3 days.
reheat: Warm just the rice for 1 minute, or eat everything cold.
tips: Season the rice with a little rice vinegar for a sushi flavour.

name: Lamb Kofta with Herbed Couscous
description: Spiced lamb skewers, lemony couscous and a cool mint yogurt.
steps: Mix lamb with cumin, two-thirds of the garlic, half the onion, 1 tsp salt and half the mint.
Shape into 12 oval koftas (thread onto skewers if you like).
Grill or broil 10–12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked to 71°C / 160°F.
Pour 1¼ cups boiling water over the couscous, cover 5 minutes, then fluff with lemon juice and salt.
Stir the remaining garlic and mint into the yogurt.
Divide couscous, koftas, cucumber, tomatoes and remaining onion into containers.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days, yogurt sauce separate. Freeze cooked koftas for up to 3 months.
reheat: Microwave koftas and couscous 1½–2 minutes; add the cold salad and sauce after.
tips: Ground beef or a beef-lamb mix makes a milder kofta.

name: Italian Sausage & Peppers Orzo
description: One-pot orzo with sweet peppers, tomato and parmesan.
steps: Brown sausage in a deep skillet over medium-high heat, about 6 minutes; remove.
Cook peppers and onion in the drippings for 5 minutes until softened; add garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in orzo, tomatoes, broth and basil and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook 10–12 minutes, stirring twice, until the orzo is tender.
Return sausage to the pan and stir in parmesan.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days.
reheat: Add a splash of water and microwave 2 minutes.
tips: Chicken sausage makes it lighter.

name: Bacon & Egg Breakfast Burritos
description: Freezer burritos stuffed with eggs, crispy potatoes, bacon and cheddar.
steps: Cook bacon in a large skillet until crisp; remove and leave 1 tbsp fat in the pan.
Fry potatoes in the fat for 12–15 minutes until golden and tender; season with salt and pepper.
Add spinach and cook until wilted.
Whisk eggs and scramble softly in the same pan, then fold in bacon.
Cool the filling 10 minutes so it doesn't steam the tortillas.
Fill each tortilla with filling, cheddar and a spoon of salsa; roll tightly and wrap in foil.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days, or freeze wrapped burritos in a bag for up to 3 months.
reheat: Remove foil, wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave 1 minute (2–3 minutes from frozen), flipping halfway.
tips: Warm the tortillas before rolling so they don't crack.

name: Cashew Chicken Stir-Fry
description: Crunchy cashews, snap peas and peppers in a glossy hoisin sauce.
steps: Cook jasmine rice.
Toast cashews in a dry wok for 2–3 minutes until golden; set aside.
Toss chicken with cornstarch, then stir-fry in oil over high heat for 5–6 minutes.
Add pepper and snap peas and cook 2–3 minutes until crisp-tender.
Stir in garlic, ginger, soy sauce, hoisin and 3 tbsp water; simmer 1 minute until glossy.
Fold in the cashews and serve over rice.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days.
reheat: Microwave 2 minutes, stirring halfway.
tips: Pack the cashews separately if you want them to stay crunchy.

name: Cajun Tilapia with Cauliflower Rice
description: Low-carb, high-protein and on the table in 25 minutes.
steps: Pat tilapia dry and rub both sides with cajun seasoning.
Sear in 1 tbsp hot oil for 3 minutes per side until it flakes easily.
In a second skillet, sauté pepper and corn in the remaining oil for 3 minutes.
Add cauliflower rice and cook 5 minutes until tender but not mushy; season with salt.
Stir cilantro into the cauliflower rice and divide with the fish and lime wedges.
storage: Fridge up to 3 days.
reheat: Microwave at 50% power for 2 minutes; squeeze over the lime after heating.
tips: Frozen riced cauliflower is fine — cook off the extra moisture first.

name: Maple Pecan Baked Oatmeal Cups
description: Soft, cinnamon-y oatmeal muffins with apple and toasted pecans.
steps: Heat oven to 180°C / 350°F and grease or line a 12-cup muffin tin.
Whisk milk, eggs, maple syrup, cinnamon, baking powder and a pinch of salt.
Stir in oats, apple and most of the pecans.
Divide between the cups and sprinkle with the remaining pecans.
Bake 22–25 minutes until set and golden; cool 10 minutes before removing.
storage: Fridge up to 5 days, or freeze for up to 3 months.
reheat: Microwave 30 seconds (1 minute from frozen).
tips: Use oat milk and flax eggs to make it vegan.

name: Pesto Pasta Salad with Mozzarella & Pistachios
description: A cold pasta salad that doesn't get soggy — perfect for desk lunches.
steps: Cook pasta in well-salted water until al dente.
Drain and rinse under cold water until cool; shake dry.
Toss pasta with pesto and lemon juice.
Fold in mozzarella and tomatoes.
Divide into containers and top with arugula and pistachios.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days.
reheat: No reheating — serve cold or at room temperature.
tips: Keep a little extra pesto to refresh the salad on day three or four.

name: Spinach Ricotta Stuffed Shells
description: Cheesy baked shells that freeze in perfect portions.
ingredients: 10 oz frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
steps: Heat oven to 190°C / 375°F.
Boil shells 2 minutes less than the package says; drain and lay flat on an oiled tray.
Mix ricotta, half the mozzarella, half the parmesan, egg, spinach, garlic and pepper.
Spread 1 cup marinara in the baking dish, fill each shell with a heaped spoon of filling and arrange on top.
Cover with the remaining sauce and cheese, then foil.
Bake 25 minutes covered and 10 minutes uncovered until bubbling.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days, or freeze portions for up to 3 months.
reheat: Microwave 2½ minutes covered, or bake from frozen at 180°C / 350°F for 40 minutes.
tips: Squeeze the spinach really dry — wet spinach makes a watery filling.

name: Thai Green Curry Shrimp
description: Fragrant coconut curry with shrimp, zucchini and basil.
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
steps: Cook jasmine rice.
Fry curry paste in a splash of oil for 1 minute until fragrant.
Whisk in coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add zucchini and pepper and cook 5 minutes.
Add shrimp and simmer 3–4 minutes until pink.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice and basil; serve over rice.
storage: Fridge up to 3 days.
reheat: Microwave 2 minutes at 70% power so the shrimp stay tender.
tips: Curry paste brands vary a lot in heat — start with 2 tbsp and taste.

name: Vegan Lentil Bolognese
description: Rich, meaty-tasting lentil ragù over whole wheat spaghetti.
steps: Sauté onion, carrot and celery in oil for 8–10 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add garlic and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes, stirring.
Add lentils, crushed tomatoes, broth and Italian seasoning.
Simmer partly covered for 30–35 minutes until the lentils are tender and the sauce is thick.
Cook spaghetti until al dente and divide with the sauce.
storage: Fridge up to 5 days. Freeze the sauce alone for up to 4 months.
reheat: Microwave 2½ minutes with a splash of water.
tips: A teaspoon of soy sauce or miso adds even more savoury depth.

name: Chicken Tikka Masala
description: Yogurt-marinated chicken in a creamy spiced tomato sauce.
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless skinless chicken thighs, cubed
steps: Toss chicken with yogurt, half the garam masala and 1 tsp salt; marinate at least 20 minutes (or overnight).
Sear chicken in batches in a hot oiled pan until charred in spots; set aside.
Cook onion for 6 minutes, then add garlic, ginger and the remaining garam masala for 1 minute.
Add tomato sauce and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in cream and the chicken and simmer 10 minutes until cooked through.
Serve with basmati rice.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freeze the curry without rice for up to 3 months.
reheat: Microwave 2½ minutes, stirring halfway.
tips: Coconut cream instead of heavy cream makes it dairy-free if you also skip the yogurt.

name: Mason Jar Cobb Salads
description: Chicken, bacon, egg and blue cheese, layered so the lettuce stays crisp.
steps: Season chicken and cook in a skillet 6–7 minutes per side until 74°C / 165°F; cool and dice.
Cook bacon until crisp, drain on paper towels and crumble.
Boil eggs 10 minutes, cool in ice water, peel and chop.
Layer each jar from the bottom: vinaigrette, tomatoes, chicken, egg, bacon, blue cheese, then lettuce on top.
Seal and refrigerate upright.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days, standing upright so the dressing stays at the bottom.
reheat: No reheating — shake into a bowl and toss.
tips: Dry the lettuce thoroughly; a salad spinner makes the jars last longer.

name: Korean Beef Bulgogi Bowls
description: Sweet-savory ground beef with gochujang, rice, cucumber and kimchi.
steps: Cook rice.
Whisk soy sauce, brown sugar, gochujang and sesame oil.
Brown beef in a skillet over high heat for 6–7 minutes, breaking it up; drain excess fat.
Add garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the sauce; simmer 2 minutes until sticky.
Divide rice and beef into containers with cucumber, kimchi and green onions in separate sections.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Keep the kimchi in its own small container.
reheat: Microwave the rice and beef 2 minutes; add cucumber and kimchi cold.
tips: A fried or jammy egg on top makes it a bibimbap-style bowl.

name: Mango Coconut Chia Pudding
description: A creamy, tropical, no-cook vegan breakfast.
steps: Whisk coconut milk, almond milk, maple syrup and vanilla in a bowl.
Whisk in the chia seeds.
Rest 10 minutes and whisk again to break up any clumps.
Divide into jars, top with mango and refrigerate at least 4 hours.
storage: Fridge up to 5 days.
reheat: No reheating — eat cold.
tips: Swap mango for pineapple or berries.

name: Mediterranean Tuna & White Bean Salad
description: A no-cook, high-protein lunch built from the pantry.
ingredients: 2 (15 oz) cans cannellini beans, rinsed and drained
steps: Whisk lemon juice, olive oil, mustard, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add beans, cucumber, onion, olives and parsley and toss.
Gently fold in the tuna, keeping some chunks.
Divide into containers.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days.
reheat: No reheating — serve cold, on greens or with crackers.
tips: Oil-packed tuna is richer; drain it well.

name: Slow Cooker Pork Carnitas Burrito Bowls
description: Citrusy pulled pork crisped under the broiler, with rice, beans and pico.
ingredients: 2.5 lbs pork shoulder, cut into chunks
1 (15 oz) can pinto beans, rinsed and drained
steps: Rub pork with cumin, oregano and 2 tsp salt.
Put onion and garlic in the slow cooker, add the pork and pour over the orange and lime juice.
Cook on low 8 hours until it shreds easily.
Shred the pork, spread on a sheet pan, drizzle with some cooking juices and broil 4–5 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Cook rice and warm the beans.
Divide rice, beans and carnitas into containers; pack pico separately.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freeze the carnitas with some juices for up to 3 months.
reheat: Microwave 2½ minutes; add pico after heating.
tips: Save the cooking liquid — it keeps the pork moist when reheated.

name: Cajun Shrimp & Sausage Sheet Pan
description: A Louisiana-style boil without the pot.
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
steps: Heat oven to 220°C / 425°F.
Toss potatoes with half the oil and seasoning and roast 15 minutes.
Add sausage, corn and zucchini, toss with the remaining oil and seasoning and roast 8 minutes.
Add shrimp and roast 6–7 minutes more until pink.
Squeeze over lemon and divide into containers.
storage: Fridge up to 3 days.
reheat: Microwave 2 minutes at 70% power.
tips: Smoked kielbasa works if you can't find andouille.

name: Turkey Taco Stuffed Peppers
description: Bell peppers filled with spiced turkey, rice, beans and melted cheddar.
ingredients: 4 large bell peppers, tops cut off and seeded
1 (15 oz) can black beans, rinsed and drained
steps: Heat oven to 190°C / 375°F and stand the peppers in a baking dish.
Brown turkey with cumin, chili powder and salt for 7 minutes.
Stir in rice, beans and salsa.
Pack the filling into the peppers, add 3 tbsp water to the dish and cover with foil.
Bake 25 minutes, uncover, top with cheddar and bake 10 minutes more.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days, or freeze individually for up to 3 months.
reheat: Microwave 2–3 minutes covered.
tips: Microwave the empty peppers for 3 minutes first if you like them very soft.

name: Miso-Glazed Salmon with Bok Choy
description: Caramelized miso salmon, garlicky greens and brown rice.
steps: Cook brown rice.
Whisk miso, honey and rice vinegar and brush over the salmon.
Broil salmon 8–10 minutes on a lined sheet pan until caramelized and just cooked.
Sauté bok choy cut side down with garlic for 3–4 minutes until the stems are tender.
Divide rice, salmon and bok choy; top with sesame seeds and scallions.
storage: Fridge up to 3 days.
reheat: Microwave at 50% power for 2 minutes, or eat the salmon cold.
tips: Watch the broiler closely — the miso glaze burns quickly.

name: Butternut Squash Mac & Cheese
description: Creamy, veg-packed mac with hidden squash and broccoli.
steps: Simmer squash in salted water for 12–15 minutes until very tender; drain.
Blend squash with milk, butter and mustard until smooth.
Cook macaroni, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes; drain.
Return pasta to the pot, pour in the squash sauce and stir in the cheddar over low heat until melted.
Season with salt and divide into containers.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 2 months.
reheat: Add a splash of milk and microwave 2 minutes, stirring halfway.
tips: Frozen cubed squash saves a lot of peeling.

name: Egg Roll in a Bowl
description: All the flavour of an egg roll, none of the wrapper. Low-carb and fast.
steps: Brown pork in a large skillet for 6–7 minutes, breaking it up.
Add garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute.
Add coleslaw mix and carrot and stir-fry 4–5 minutes until just wilted.
Stir in soy sauce, sesame oil and sriracha.
Top with green onions and divide into containers.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days.
reheat: Microwave 1½–2 minutes.
tips: Use tamari instead of soy sauce to make it gluten-free.

name: Mediterranean Hummus Snack Boxes
description: Bento-style boxes for lunches that need zero reheating.
ingredients: 4 whole wheat pitas, cut into wedges
steps: Boil eggs 10 minutes, cool in ice water and peel.
Cut cucumber into rounds and carrots into sticks.
Spoon hummus into small lidded cups.
Divide pita, eggs, vegetables, olives and feta between the boxes.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Keep pita in a separate bag if you like it soft.
reheat: No reheating — eat cold.
tips: Toast the pita wedges into chips for extra crunch.
